Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Setup 3 Gameplay 3.1 Types of Cards 3.2 Terms 3.3 Turn Steps 4 Winning 5 Variants 5.1 Mode 5.2 Legends 5.3 Garage Module 5.4 Weather and Road Conditions 5.5 Tunnel Vision 5.6 Heavy Rain 5.7 Features on Expansion Maps Overview Pedal to the Metal is a game of hand management, deckbuilding, and "push your luck". Racing isn't just going as fast as you can. It's managing your speed, engine heat, and adrenaline. After a set number of laps, be the first to cross the finish line and win! Each player has their own deck of cards, from which they draw a hand, and a player board. The player board indicates your car's current status, including your gear shift. Your gear shift indicates how many cards you can play that round. The value of the cards played indicates your speed, which is how many spaces you can move along the race track. Playing high-value cards will make you go faster, but if you have too much speed or take a turn too fast, your engine will overheat, you'll spin out, and you'll lose a turn. Setup Every player's deck starts with 12 Basic Cards (3 x 1 , 3 x 2 , 3 x 3 , 3 x 4 , some Stress cards, and some Starting Upgrade cards. The number of Stress and Starting Upgrade cards depends on the track (3 each for the USA track). A supply of Heat cards is placed next to your player board (6 for the USA track). The gear shift starts at 1. Each player draws 7 cards to their hand to start. Gameplay Heat: Pedal to the Metal is played over several rounds. Some steps will be taken every turn, some are situational. All players complete steps 1 and 2 simultaneously. Then the player with the frontmost car closest to the Race Line (inside of the track) completes their remaining steps and finishes their turn. Then the player with the next closest car goes, and so on until all players have completed their turn. Then the round ends. This sequence continues until all cars have finished the race. Steps in a Turn Step Status Shift Gears Play Cards Reveal Cards & Move Car Adrenaline Situational React Situational Slipstream Situational Check Corner Situational Discard Situational Replenish Hand Types of Cards Basic These cards represent your car's Speed during this round. When played, the values of all Basic cards are added together. That number represents how many spaces your car moves forward. Stress These cards represent lapses of concentration as you race around the track. All players start with three in their deck. Stress cards cannot be discarded. To get them out of your hand, they have to be played, which adds some randomness to your Speed. Upgrade Upgrade cards are indicated by a blue chevron symbol in the upper corners. Note that these cards are discarded when the is activated, even if the card has a number. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] The more I play it, the less I like it. Now at the point where I wouldn't want to see it again.   Ends up being 'boring' - aren't racing games supposed to be fun.

[Rating: 1/10] One of the most boring games I've ever played. If the objective was to realistically simulate a race they nailed it because you spend most of the game doing things that have zero impact only to decide the whole race's outcome on that last stretch over the finish line. I tried to play this live and found it incredibly dull so gave it another shot on BGA... I literally fell asleep on my laptop. Can't understand what all the hype is about but fanboys will go absolutely nuts if you so much as disagree that this game is a masterpiece.

[Rating: 1/10] The more I play, the less I enjoy it. Not as much strategic depth as there originally seemed. I understand it's a 'tactical' game first and foremost, but even there it is lacking in terms of satisfying decision space. You will generally fall victim to luck of the draw, and based on your hand at any given moment, the choice(s) you should be making are fairly obvious, almost autonomous. Sure, there is the occasional decision of 'should I push my luck with this Stress card to advance a little further' but even then, those choices become more transparent the more you play. I won't turn down a game

[Rating: 1/10] I do not get the love for this game… played on BGA and was extremely underwhelmed. Very thankful I didn’t jump on the FOMO train and fork out a ridiculous amount of money for this before playing it.

[Rating: 1/10] impossible to stop a run-away winner. too much luck involved. too slow initial drafting (esp. for a racing game). very narrow decision-space. sadly, definitely not worth the hype...

[Rating: 1/10] I did not like this game. Well put together I suppose but nothing like what I wanted in terms of gameplay, but I dislike how it feels like there is a "give everyone a chance" catch up type feeling in the game. It felt like the start and final turn were all that mattered.

[Rating: 1/10] There are not many games that I really dislike but this is one. I just dont get the hype. It felt like monopoly with a car. It did not feel like driving a racing car. I couldnt wait for it to end.

[Rating: 1/10] [b]Racing drama built from hand constraints rather than meaningful strategic development.[/b] Heat management, corner timing, slipstreaming and gear selection create competent tactical play, but almost every decision lives only a few turns ahead. Hand composition repeatedly dictates what is possible, while Stress introduces still more uncertainty into an already narrow decision space. Garage modules add variety without changing the underlying experience: manage the cards you drew, survive the next corner, repeat. Exciting as a race; nearly barren as a strategy game.

[Rating: 1/10] It's not particularly bad at anything, just that playing it enough I realize there's very few decisions that matter (and they do, but are a minority). The deckbuilding has some avoidable lows, but very few highs. It's not as interesting as Quest for El Dorado, you're just doing busywork to manage all these sub-phases with weird order and variables. Unless you're slipstreaming, then you mindlessly move forward automatically... bypassing many of the restrictions, which means even MORE rules to learn! [Rating: 1/10] You will not convinced if you loss this game, since the luck of this is extremely high. I played 240 times on BGA and I will not recommend this game.

[Rating: 1/10] Wow, really hated this. Watching 5 people fiddling around with their small personal player deck of cards for over an hour.  I just wanted it to stop.  No real player interaction.  After one play, the decisions are obvious on what you need to do... slow around the turns and fast on the straight away.  No kidding.  And because of the deck builder aspect, it comes completely down to the card draw.  Sorry, but no.  Downforce is so much better.
